acceptanceCriteria: Camera position and orbit target are owned by exactly one controller (no component calls camera.lookAt() independently of the orbit/controls system).

Clicking any single object completes its focus transition and then remains stable: after the transition finishes and 5 seconds elapse with no further input, the camera does not jump, snap, or reorient again.
Rapidly clicking 10 different objects in quick succession results in the camera settling stably on the last-clicked object, with no oscillation between targets.

User-initiated orbit/drag interaction during or after a focus transition is respected (does not fight with or get overridden by an in-flight programmatic transition in a jarring way) and does not leave the camera in a broken/unreachable state.

The guided tour's camera movement between scenes continues to work using the same single controller, and prefers-reduced-motion still results in an instant (non-animated) camera cut rather than a lerp.

Automated regression tests exist for: single-click focus settles and stays settled, rapid multi-click settles on the final target, and reduced-motion produces an immediate camera position without an animated transition.

npm ci, lint, typecheck, unit tests, Playwright e2e (including the new camera regression coverage), and the static export build all succeed; existing v0.2/v0.2.1 behavior (Governance Loop scene, three modes, i18n) is not regressed.
goal: Replace the split ArchitectureCamera + OrbitControls ownership with a single camera controller (drei CameraControls, using setLookAt for focus transitions) so camera position and target are always owned by exactly one system. No regression in existing focus-on-select, tour camera movement, or reduced-motion behavior.
intent: Fix the P0 camera bug where ArchitectureCamera manually calls camera.lookAt() while a separate OrbitControls owns its own independent target, causing the camera to visibly snap/flicker back on the next OrbitControls update after every focus transition.
outOfScope: Changing the Governance Loop semantic model or i18n content
